newsitem.title: MEXICO: Halt of Mexican corruption probe angers opponents.
newsitem.headline: Halt of Mexican corruption probe angers opponents.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Thursday came under fierce attack from opposition lawmakers, who accused him of covering up a corruption scandal at the highest levels of government.

Rancorous debate in the lower-house Chamber of Deputies followed a decision by the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) to shut down a congressional investigation into the government's troubled Conasupo food subsidy programme which allegedly embroiled Zedillo himself.
The PRI majority on a special commission probing the agency voted on Wednesday to shut itself down, blaming only a few low-level Conasupo officials for irregularities.
The full Chamber, also dominated by the PRI, was expected to follow suit later on Thursday in a vote after the debate.

Opposition congressmen alleged that Zedillo, while Budget and Planning Minister in 1989, acquiesced to an illegal $7 million payment from Conasupo to Maseca, the tortilla and corn-flour giant. Zedillo's office vigorously denied the charges.

The leftist Democratic Revolution Party and conservative National Action Party also alleged that corruption in Conasupo was one of the sources of the huge fortune accumulated by Raul Salinas de Gortari, the brother of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari.
Raul Salinas is in jail on murder and corruption charges. Investigators have uncovered as much as $300 million that he had allegedly stashed in secret European bank accounts.

Allegations of corruption against the long-ruling PRI are nothing new, but Zedillo, a bespectacled technocrat with a relatively clean image, has never before been subject to such broad and direct attacks.

"Those responsible for this document are not the PRI deputies on the commission," independent congressman Adolfo Aguilar Zinser said during the debate, referring to the PRI-dominated commission's closing report.
"It was Ernesto Zedillo Ponce de Leon, president of the republic," he added to applause. "I accuse him!"
PRI congressmen defended shutting down the probe, saying it was thorough and was being questioned merely because it did not meet the political objectives of the opposition.
"We in the PRI want justice, not vengeance," said Juan Manuel Cruz Acevedo, also a member of the commission. "The PRI does not cover up for anybody. The coverup is only in the minds of sick people."
